steps.body: Pair six grapes with six of Ben's seven grapes. The one unmatched grape shows which group has more.
steps.narration: Pair six grapes with six of Ben's seven grapes. The one unmatched grape shows which group has more.

widget.prompt: Pair 5 hearts with stars, one each — then show the stars used.

commonCounts.feedback: Four stars leave one heart unmatched; the pairing is not finished.
Six stars is one more than the hearts need; one star would stand alone.

widget.missFeedback: Give each heart exactly one star and stop when the hearts run out.
widget.successFeedback: Five stars for five hearts — the pairing comes out perfectly even.

predict.prompt: Pairing 5 hearts with 5 stars, what remains at the end?
predict.reveal: Equal groups use each other up exactly — pair 5 hearts with 6 stars instead, and one star stands alone.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm match pairs.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm match pairs uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: After pairing, two hearts stand unmatched. What does that show?

options.label: Two hearts were counted wrong
options.feedback: Nothing was miscounted; leftovers are what pairing is designed to reveal.

options.label: There are two more hearts than stars
options.feedback: Correct — every star found a heart, and the two spare hearts are exactly the difference.

options.label: The stars are bigger
options.feedback: Pairing says nothing about size — it measures which group has more members.

options.label: The groups are equal anyway
options.feedback: Equal groups pair off with nothing spare; two leftovers mean the hearts outnumber.

widget.prompt: There are 3 stars and 4 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Equal needs the pairing to come out even; here one side is left holding extras (3 against 4).

options.label: More stars
options.feedback: Pairing one to one uses every star with hearts to spare, so the stars are not the larger group.

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Correct — 4 hearts against 3 stars; pairing one to one leaves hearts unmatched.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and look at which side has leftovers.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 10 to land on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 2 on from 10: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 2 more is 12 — every step forward lands on a greater number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts are needed to reach 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 12.
